learning_objective: 🎯 Master the art of manipulating text! Learn how to slice, join, and modify strings of characters in Python.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A string is a sequence of characters enclosed in single quotes ('hello'), double quotes ("hello"), or triple quotes ('''hello'''). It is treated as text data.
Every character in a string has a position called an index. Forward indexing starts at 0 (first character). Backward (negative) indexing starts at -1 (last character).
Once a string is created, you cannot change its individual characters. `word[0] = 'H'` will throw an error! You must create a completely new string instead.
You can extract a substring using slicing: `string_name[start : stop : step]`. It extracts characters from the 'start' index up to, but not including, the 'stop' index.
Python provides built-in methods to manipulate strings, such as `.upper()` (converts to uppercase), `.lower()`, `.replace()`, and `.split()`.

fun_activity.title: ✂️ The String Ninja
fun_activity.instructions: If `word = "COMPUTER"`, what will `word[0:4]` output? (Hint: It grabs characters from index 0 up to 3). Try guessing what `word[::-1]` does! (It reverses the string!).

exam_tips: 📌 Indexing out of bounds (trying to access an index that doesn't exist) will cause an `IndexError`.
📌 Remember that the `stop` value in a slice `[start:stop]` is always excluded.
📌 `+` concatenates (joins) two strings, while `*` replicates (repeats) a string a certain number of times.
quick_recap: ⭐ The `len()` function returns the total number of characters in a string, including spaces.
⭐ Strings can be iterated over using a `for` loop.
⭐ The `in` and `not in` operators can check if a substring exists within another string.
